accepted.question_text: If n>2 and Λ is a lattice in R^(n+1) with positive homogeneous minimum N(Λ)=inf{|z0z1···zn| : z∈Λ\{0}} > 0, must Λ be an algebraic lattice? This is the higher-dimensional Oppenheim conjecture discussed in the paper.

evidence.quote: A famous Oppenheim conjecture supposes that in the case n > 2 any lattice Λ satisfying N (L) > 0 is an algebraic lattice. This conjecture is still open.

accepted.question_text: Given two distinct weight triples (α1,β1,γ1) and (α2,β2,γ2) in [0,1]^3 with αi+βi+γi=1, must the intersection BAD(α1,β1,γ1) ∩ BAD(α2,β2,γ2) be nonempty? Here BAD(α,β,γ) denotes the set of triples (θ1,θ2,θ3) for which inf_p max{p^α||pθ1||, p^β||pθ2||, p^γ||pθ3||} stays positive.

accepted.question_text: In the inhomogeneous multiplicative approximation setting of Theorem 8, can one choose the auxiliary function ψ to be a positive constant ψ(t)=ψ0 for all t and still obtain real numbers θ1,θ2 that are linearly independent with 1, together with real shifts η1,η2, such that inf over positive integers x of x·ψ0·||xθ1−η1||·||xθ2−η2|| remains positive? If this is impossible, the paper notes that a stronger inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture would follow.

evidence.quote:
The following problem is an open one: is it possible that for a constant function ψ(t) = ψ0 > 0 ∀t
the conclusion of Theorem 8 remains true. If not, it means that a stronger inhomogeneous version of
Littlewood conjecture is valid.

accepted.question_text: For weights α,β in (0,1) with α+β=1 and an arbitrary fixed pair (θ1,θ2)∈R^2, does the inhomogeneous badly approximable set {(η1,η2)∈R^2 : inf_q max(q^α||qθ1−η1||, q^β||qθ2−η2||) > 0} always have full Hausdorff dimension, and is it even a winning set, without assuming that (θ1,θ2) lies in BAD(α,β)?

evidence.quote:

accepted.question_text: For lacunary sequences satisfying the growth condition t_{j+1}/t_j > 1+1/M, what is the correct order of approximation in the homogeneous problem of bounding ||α t_j|| away from zero uniformly in j? More specifically, can the lower bound in Peres–Schlag’s theorem be improved to the optimal order, rather than the current γ/(M log M) scale?

evidence.quote:
The open
question is to find the right order of approximation in the homogeneous version of this problem. In
general Peres-Schlag’s method does not give optimal bounds. The conjecture is that Theorem 9 may
be improved on, and the optimal result should be stronger than the inequality (11).

accepted.question_text: For weights α,β in (0,1) with α+β=1 and (α,β)≠(1/2,1/2), is the weighted badly approximable set BAD(α,β) a winning set in Schmidt’s game sense? More generally, the paper asks for the winning properties of sets produced by the Peres–Schlag method and the Badziahin–Pollington–Velani method.

evidence.quote: Moreover we do not know if the set BAD(α, β) is a winning set in the case (α, β) 6= (1/2, 1/2). ... I would be very interesting to study winning properties of the sets arising from Peres-Schlag’s method and Badziahin-Pollington-Velani’s method.

accepted.question_text: What are the optimal exponents in Thurnheer’s approximation problems from large domains Φ and Ψ? In particular, are the parameter choices in formulas (43) and (45) optimal for obtaining (44) and (46), and what is the optimal value of s(ρ) ensuring infinitely many integer solutions to (48)?

evidence.quote:
4. What are optimal exponents in the Thurnheer’s setting for large domains Φ, Ψ? In particular,
are the values of parameters ρ, τ from (43) and (45) optimal to get (44) and (46) or not? What is
the optimal values of s(ρ) to conclude that (48) has infinitely many solutions in integers (x1, x2)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant k such that for every positive integer q there is some numerator a coprime to q whose continued fraction a/q=[b0;b1,…,bs] has all partial quotients bounded by k? The paper notes Zaremba’s stronger conjecture that one may take k=5, and perhaps even k=2 for large prime q.

evidence.quote:
The famous Zaremba’s conjecture [154] supposes that there exists an absolute constant k with the
following property: for any positive integer q there exists a coprime to q such that in the continued
fraction expansion (53) all partial quotients are bounded... In fact Zaremba conjectured that k = 5. Probably for large prime q even k = 2 sould be enough

accepted.question_text: Can the Bourgain–Kontorovich proof toward Zaremba’s conjecture be simplified so that one avoids the difficult spectral-theoretic input from Bourgain–Kontorovich–Sarnak, perhaps using more elementary estimates such as Weil bounds for Kloosterman sums at least for a positive-proportion result?

evidence.quote:
I think that it is possible to simplify the proof given by Bourgain and Kontorovich and to avoid the
application of a difficult result from [12]. Probably for a certain positive proportion result A. Weil’s
estimates on Kloosterman sums should be enough.
